session.question: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
session.answer:
Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) was evaluated as a solid lubricant nano-additive in canola oil to enhance its tribological performance. The study focused on assessing the impact of various hBN concentrations on the lubricant's efficacy, identifying 1.0 wt.% as the optimal concentration that yielded a 40% reduction in coefficient of friction (COF) compared to the base oil. The experiments employed a pin on disk test, specifically characterizing the lubricant behavior within the boundary lubrication regime (unknownauthorsUnknownyearsynergisticstudyof chunk 1).

Further investigations into the synergistic effects of combining hBN with graphene nanoplatelets (GNP) revealed improved performance metrics. The mixture of hBN and GNP in different ratios achieved a notable reduction in friction by 56% and a decrease in wear by 90% relative to the base oil. This combination highlights the potential of hBN not only as a singular additive but also in conjunction with other nano-materials to significantly enhance the tribological properties of canola oil, positioning it as a sustainable bio-lubricant option (unknownauthorsUnknownyearsynergisticstudyof chunk 1).
